title: Saturated Kummer pushouts and their finite monoid-algebra realization
statement:
Let $P,Q,R$ be fine saturated commutative monoids, written additively [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Let $h:P\to Q$ be injective with each $q\in Q$ having a positive multiple in $h(P)$, and suppose $h^{\rm gp}$ is injective with finite cokernel $C$ annihilated by $n\geq1$. Let $a:P\to R$ be any homomorphism. Form $S_0=Q\oplus_P R$, the quotient of $Q\oplus R$ by the congruence identifying $(h(p),0)$ and $(0,a(p))$. Its integralization $S_{\rm int}$ is its image in $S_0^{\rm gp}$, and its saturation is
$$S=\{u\in S_0^{\rm gp}:mu\in S_{\rm int}\text{ for some integer }m>0\}.$$
Then $S$ is fine saturated, $R\to S$ and $R^{\rm gp}\to S^{\rm gp}$ are injective, every element of $S$ has a positive multiple in $R$, and the canonical group cokernel is $S^{\rm gp}/R^{\rm gp}\cong C$. The monoid $S$ is the pushout of $Q\leftarrow P\to R$ among fine saturated monoids. Write $\mathbf Z[M]$ for the ring with abelian basis $z^m$ and multiplication $z^mz^{m'}=z^{m+m'}$. For every commutative $\mathbf Z[R]$-algebra $A$ in which $n$ is invertible, the ring maps
$$A\longrightarrow A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[R]}\mathbf Z[S],\qquad
A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[R]}\mathbf Z[S_0]\longrightarrow A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[R]}\mathbf Z[S]$$
are finite and induce surjective maps of spectra. These statements hold after arbitrary further scalar extension. Tensor products and spectra are as in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For fs log structures with compatible charts $P,Q,R$, the fs fibre product is obtained from the ordinary scheme fibre product $F$ by the chart construction
$$F\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[S_0]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[S],$$
with the log structure associated to $S$. This construction, characterized by compatible maps of the three log sheaves, commutes with restriction of charts and is the fibre product in fs log schemes. Such charts exist locally: for a morphism $g:(Y',N')\to(Y,N)$ of fs log schemes, a chart $P\to N$ on an etale neighbourhood of $g(\bar y')$ and a geometric point $\bar y'$ of $Y'$, there are a pointed etale neighbourhood of $\bar y'$, an fs monoid $R$ with a chart $R\to N'$ on it, and a homomorphism $a:P\to R$ compatible with $g$. Here on arbitrary schemes a log structure is a sheaf of commutative monoids with a structural map to $\mathcal O$ inducing an isomorphism on units, and fs means admitting etale-local charts by fine saturated monoids, as in [def-trf-log-ideal-chart-presentation]. No Noetherian or flatness assumption on $A$ or on the charted schemes is made.

source.place: VI 2.1--2.2, pp.71--72, algebra of standard Kummer covers; VIII 3.3.5 and 3.3.9--3.3.11, pp.107--108, chart base change and saturation; X 1.8, diagram (1.a) and the fs-base-change assertion, pp.146--147. Algebraic chart formulation of these constructions.

proof.text: Put $H=(Q^{\rm gp}\oplus R^{\rm gp})/\{(h^{\rm gp}(p),-a^{\rm gp}(p)):p\in P^{\rm gp}\}$. The presentations of group completion and of $S_0$ identify $S_0^{\rm gp}=H$: maps from either presentation to any abelian group are exactly compatible pairs of maps from $Q,R$. If $(0,r)=(h^{\rm gp}(p),-a^{\rm gp}(p))$, injectivity of $h^{\rm gp}$ gives $p=0,r=0$. Thus $R^{\rm gp}\to H$ is injective, and quotienting by its image leaves exactly $Q^{\rm gp}/h^{\rm gp}(P^{\rm gp})=C$. The image $S_{\rm int}$ is generated by the images of finite generating sets of $Q,R$ and generates $H$ as a group.

source.place: VI 2.1--2.2, pp.71--72; algebraic verification of the Kummer chart construction

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fine-monoid-finite-saturation] to the integral finitely generated monoid $S_{\rm int}\subset H$. Its saturation is the displayed $S$, is fs, and has group completion $H$. The injections $R\subset R^{\rm gp}\subset H$ land in $S$. For $s\in S$ choose $m>0$ with $ms=q+r$ in $H$. Choose $d>0,p\in P$ with $dq=h(p)$. Then $dm s=a(p)+dr\in R$. This proves the positive-multiple assertion, including torsion elements, and the first step gives the asserted cokernel.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17, p.101, and 3.2.9, p.104 (finite saturation); VI 2.1, p.71

proof.text: If $T$ is fs and $Q\to T$, $R\to T$ agree on $P$, the monoid presentation gives $S_0\to T$. Since $T\to T^{\rm gp}$ is injective this factors through $S_{\rm int}$. The induced group map $H\to T^{\rm gp}$ sends $s\in S$ into $T$: a positive multiple of its image belongs to $T$ and $T$ is saturated. Its restriction $S\to T$ is the required extension. Any extension has that group map, because $S_{\rm int}$ generates $H$, so it is unique. This proves the fs monoid pushout property.

source.place: VI 2.1--2.2, pp.71--72; algebraic verification of the Kummer chart construction

proof.text: Let $s_1,\ldots,s_t$ generate $S$ and choose $d_i>0$ with $d_i s_i\in R$ by Step 2. Every monomial in $\mathbf Z[S]$ is a product of an $R$-monomial and one of the finitely many $z^{\sum e_i s_i}$, $0\le e_i<d_i$, by division with remainder of the exponents. These monomials span $\mathbf Z[S]$ over $\mathbf Z[R]$ and also over $\mathbf Z[S_0]$ (whose image contains $\mathbf Z[R]$). After tensoring with $A$ the same finite spanning formulas prove both claimed ring maps finite. This argument does not require flatness, Noetherianity, or invertibility of $n$.

source.place: VI 2.1--2.2, pp.71--72; algebraic verification of the Kummer chart construction

proof.text: For use in lifting points, record a face calculation. A face of an additive monoid is a submonoid $F$ such that $x+y\in F$ implies $x,y\in F$. If $P\to Q$ is our Kummer injection and $F_P=h^{-1}(F_Q)$ for a face $F_Q$ of $Q$, then $q\in F_Q$ exactly when $dq=h(p)$ for some $d>0,p\in F_P$: one implication uses a Kummer multiple; the other uses the face property. Moreover $(h^{\rm gp})^{-1}(F_Q^{\rm gp})=F_P^{\rm gp}$. Indeed, write $h^{\rm gp}(u)=q_1-q_2$ with $q_i\in F_Q$, choose a common $d>0$ with $dq_i=h(p_i)$, $p_i\in F_P$, and obtain $du=p_1-p_2$. By [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening], $P^{\rm gp}/F_P^{\rm gp}$ is free abelian, hence has no nonzero element killed by $d$. Thus $u\in F_P^{\rm gp}$.

source.place: VI 2.1, p.71; VIII 3.1.1--3.1.5, pp.98--99 (face localization and sharpening)

proof.text: Take compatible monoid maps $\chi_Q:Q\to(k,\cdot)$ and $\chi_R:R\to(k,\cdot)$, where $k$ is algebraically closed. Their nonzero loci $F_Q,F_R$ are faces, with common inverse-image face $F_P\subset P$. Set $F_S=\{s\in S:ms\in F_R\text{ for some }m>0\}$, interpreting $F_R\subset H$. Every $s$ has a positive multiple in $R$. Taking common multiples shows $F_S$ is a face: if $s+t$ has a multiple in $F_R$, choose a common multiple also placing $s,t$ in $R$, and apply the face property in $R$. Its inverse image in $R$ is $F_R$, since $R\to H$ is injective and faces are root-closed inside $R$. Its inverse image in $Q$ is $F_Q$: for $dq=h(p)$, membership of the image of $q$ is equivalent successively to $a(p)\in F_R$, $p\in F_P$, and $q\in F_Q$.

source.place: VI 2.1--2.2, pp.71--72; algebraic verification of the Kummer chart construction

proof.text: The group $K=F_Q^{\rm gp}\oplus_{F_P^{\rm gp}}F_R^{\rm gp}$ maps injectively into $H$. To check the kernel, if $(q,r)$ in the sum of face groups equals $(h^{\rm gp}(u),-a^{\rm gp}(u))$ in $Q^{\rm gp}\oplus R^{\rm gp}$, Step 5 gives $u\in F_P^{\rm gp}$. Thus it was already a defining relation for $K$. Its image lies in $F_S^{\rm gp}$. On their nonzero loci the two characters extend uniquely to group homomorphisms to $k^\times$; agreement on $F_P$ gives a character $K\to k^\times$.

source.place: VI 2.1--2.2, pp.71--72; algebraic verification of the Kummer chart construction

proof.text: The group $k^\times$ is divisible: a root of $X^m-b$, for $m>0,b\ne0$, exists by algebraic closedness and is nonzero [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Apply [lem-per-divisible-group-hom-extension] to $K\hookrightarrow F_S^{\rm gp}$, writing the target group multiplicatively, to extend that character. Give $s\in F_S$ its character value and $s\notin F_S$ value zero. Since $F_S$ is a face this is a monoid homomorphism $S\to(k,\cdot)$, and Step 6 shows its restrictions are exactly $\chi_Q,\chi_R$. This proves lifting of every compatible pair, rather than assuming that an arbitrary character of $S_0$ factors through integralization.

source.place: VI 2.1--2.2, pp.71--72; algebraic verification of the Kummer chart construction

proof.text: There is also a lift of any single character $\chi_R:R\to(k,\cdot)$. Use its nonzero face $F_R$ and the face $F_S$ defined in Step 6, whose construction only uses the positive-multiple property and $R\hookrightarrow H$. The inclusion $F_R^{\rm gp}\hookrightarrow F_S^{\rm gp}$ is injective. Divisibility of $k^\times$ and [lem-per-divisible-group-hom-extension] extend the nonzero character to $F_S^{\rm gp}$; extending by zero off the face gives the desired $S$-character.

source.place: VI 2.1--2.2, pp.71--72; algebraic verification of the Kummer chart construction

proof.text: For any prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$, map $A\to k$ into an algebraic closure of its residue field [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Step 9 supplies a compatible $S$-character, hence the explicit ring map $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[R]}\mathbf Z[S]\to k$, $a\otimes z^s\mapsto\bar a\chi_S(s)$. Its kernel is a prime over $\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Likewise, for a prime of $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[R]}\mathbf Z[S_0]$, its residue-field map into an algebraic closure gives compatible $Q,R$ characters and the prescribed $A$ map; Step 8 gives a map from the target tensor ring whose restriction is that residue-field map. Its kernel lies over the original prime. Thus both spectra maps are surjective, including the empty-spectrum case.

source.place: VI 2.1--2.2, pp.71--72; algebraic verification of the Kummer chart construction

proof.text: If $A\to A'$ is any further scalar extension, $A'$ is again a $\mathbf Z[R]$-algebra with $n$ invertible. The maps after base change identify with the same displayed maps for $A'$ by $a'\otimes(a\otimes z^s)\mapsto a'a\otimes z^s$ and its inverse $a'\otimes z^s\mapsto a'\otimes(1\otimes z^s)$; the same formulas apply with $S_0$. The finite spanning sets and prime-lifting arguments above therefore prove the assertions after arbitrary scalar extension.

source.place: VI 2.1--2.2, pp.71--72; algebraic verification of the Kummer chart construction

proof.text: We first produce compatible local charts for an arbitrary fs morphism. Restrict to the prescribed target chart and choose some fs source chart $T\to N'$ near $\bar y'$. Put $L=N'_{\bar y'}$, $U=\mathcal O_{Y',\bar y'}^\times$, $F=\{t\in T: \alpha(t)\in U\}$. By [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening], $T_F=T-F$ is fs, its units are $F^{\rm gp}$ and $B=T_F/F^{\rm gp}$ is fs sharp. By the stalk formula of [lem-per-integral-chart-logification-thickening] for the chart $T$, $T\oplus_FU=L$, hence $T_F\oplus_{F^{\rm gp}}U=L$ and $B=L/U$; $L$ is integral by [lem-per-associated-log-arbitrary-scheme]. Every image of a generator $p_i$ of $P$ can thus be written $t_i+u_i$ in $L$, $t_i\in T_F$, $u_i\in U$ (we use additive notation also for log monoids and their unit groups). Let $V\subset U$ be generated as a group by these finitely many $u_i$. Let $R$ be the image of $T_F\oplus V$ in the integral monoid $L$. It is finitely generated and integral, contains the image of $P$, and maps onto $B$.

source.place: VI 1.1, p.69; VIII 3.1.1--3.1.5 and 3.3.4, pp.98--99,107; agent construction of the compatible chart monoid

proof.text: Here $R$ is already saturated. Let $H_R$ be its generated subgroup of $L^{\rm gp}$, and $W$ the subgroup of $U$ generated by the image of $F^{\rm gp}$ and $V$. The pushout presentation of $L$ in Step 12 gives $H_R\cap U=W$: write an element as $t_1-t_2+v$; if it is a unit, $t_1,t_2$ have the same image in $B$, so their difference lies in the image of $F^{\rm gp}$. Consequently $R$ is exactly the inverse image of $B\subset B^{\rm gp}$ under $H_R\to B^{\rm gp}$: choose $t\in T_F$ with the prescribed characteristic and subtract it, leaving an element of $W\subset R^\times$. Since $B$ is saturated, this inverse image is saturated. Also $R^\times=W$, and $R\oplus_W U\to L$ is an isomorphism: it is surjective since $T_F$ and $U$ generate $L$, and equality of two images implies that the difference of their $R$ terms lies in $H_R\cap U=W$, precisely the pushout relation. Thus $R\to L$ is a stalk chart.

source.place: VI 2.1--2.2, pp.71--72; algebraic verification of the Kummer chart construction

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-prelog-stalk-chart-spreading] to $R\to L$ and its stalk-chart isomorphism. It gives an fs chart $R\to N'$ on a pointed etale neighbourhood. The germ of the original $P$-map factors through the homomorphism $a:P\to R$ constructed in Step 12. The equality clause of that same lemma, applied to the finitely generated $P$, shrinks the neighbourhood so that the two $P$-maps agree as sections. Therefore $a$ is compatible with the given morphism and target chart. All hypotheses of the spreading lemma concern finite monoids and an fs log structure; none require Noetherian schemes.

source.place: VI 1.1 and VIII 3.3.4, pp.69,107; agent finite-presentation chart argument

proof.text: On compatible charts, put $Z=F\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[S_0]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[S]$ and give it the associated log structure $L_Z(S,\beta)$ of [lem-per-integral-chart-logification-thickening], where $\beta(s)$ is the pullback of $z^s$. It is fs because $S$ is fs and charts it [lem-per-associated-log-arbitrary-scheme]. For any fs test log scheme $(T,M_T)$ with compatible maps to the original factors, their charts give compatible maps $Q,R\to\Gamma(T,M_T)$ and an underlying scheme map $v:T\to F$. The section monoid is integral saturated by [lem-per-associated-log-arbitrary-scheme]. Step 3's explicit extension argument (which uses only integrality and saturation of the target) gives a unique $\lambda:S\to\Gamma(T,M_T)$. The ring map $\mathbf Z[S]\to\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ sends $z^s$ to $\alpha(\lambda(s))$ and agrees with $v$ on $\mathbf Z[S_0]$. On affine opens of $T$ the affine-spectrum correspondence gives the unique lift to $Z$, and uniqueness makes these maps agree and glue. The universal property of [lem-per-integral-chart-logification-thickening] along this scheme map gives its unique log morphism. Conversely restricting this lift to $Q,R$ recovers the given pair. Thus this chart scheme satisfies exactly the fs fibre-product universal property.

source.place: VIII 3.3.3--3.3.6, pp.106--107; X 1.8, pp.146--147; universal-property verification

proof.text: On an affine open of $F$ the underlying ring in Step 15 is its tensor product over $\mathbf Z[S_0]$ with $\mathbf Z[S]$, by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], exactly the stated chart formula. After etale restriction or replacement of compatible charts, Step 15 again describes the same functor of fs test objects, in terms of the three log sheaves. The unique comparison maps between two such representatives are inverse, since their composites induce the identity on that functor. On triple restrictions their compositions are the unique comparison. This proves compatibility with restriction of charts. Step 14 provides compatible charts locally at every geometric point, and Step 15 proves that the displayed construction on any such charts is the fs fibre product, without a Noetherian or flatness hypothesis.
